meta.title: Operation of Hot Air Oven in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To dry crude drugs, glassware, and plant powders at controlled temperatures using forced hot air circulation to achieve the desired moisture content for standardization and storage.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for drying crude drug powders (loss on drying determination), sterilizing dry glassware, and preparation of crude drugs for analysis.
procedure: Switch on the hot air oven and set the thermostat to the required temperature: 100–105°C for most crude drugs (loss on drying); 160–180°C for dry heat glassware sterilization.
Allow the oven to reach and stabilize at the set temperature for a minimum of 30 minutes before loading (critical for accuracy of LOD determinations).
Place pre-weighed samples in labelled glass Petri dishes or crucibles — record initial weight precisely.
For crude drug drying: spread the drug powder in a thin layer (< 5 mm depth) in the Petri dish.
Load the oven without overcrowding — ensure adequate air space between samples for air circulation.
Record the loading time and temperature in the logbook.
Heat for the specified time per the pharmacopeial method (typically 2–4 hours for crude drugs; 1 hour at 160°C for glassware sterilization).
At the end of the drying period, switch off the oven; open the door slightly (2–3 cm) for 5 minutes before fully opening.
Using tongs and heat-resistant gloves, transfer samples to a desiccator immediately.
Allow samples to cool in the desiccator to room temperature (30–45 minutes) before weighing.
Weigh cooled samples on an analytical balance and record the weight.
Calculate Loss on Drying (%): LOD = [(Initial weight − Final weight) / Initial weight] × 100.
If LOD target not achieved, return to oven for further drying and repeat weighing cycle.
Record all weights, drying times, and LOD values in the laboratory register.
precautions: Do not open the oven at full temperature without partial cooling — sudden temperature change causes glass containers to crack.
Use only heat-resistant glass (borosilicate) or porcelain containers — ordinary glass may crack at high temperatures.
Never dry volatile organic solvents or flammable materials in a hot air oven — explosion risk from solvent vapours.
Wear heat-resistant gloves when handling hot materials from the oven.
Place samples in a desiccator immediately after removal to prevent moisture re-absorption before weighing.
Calibrate the oven thermostat against a calibrated thermometer placed inside the chamber.
Do not block the air circulation vents or fan with samples or aluminium foil.
Maintain regular calibration records for the thermostat.
